title: MLA L0C deferred rescale with a unified conditional drain at the scale boundary
verdict_scope: CPU protocol/algebra model only. No real deferred MixedKernel or native TF effects/completion integration is implemented. The historical model results below are not G61 device proof; current G61 remains PARTIAL even though later CANN92 static arithmetic micro-cases run successfully.
historical_device_note: The device_measurement reason below is a historical run note, not the current environment diagnosis. CANN92 host runtime is now usable, but deferred backend remains unimplemented.

AIC: pending U_l0c at the current anchor

route.invariant: U_total = U_ub + U_l0c at the SAME normalisation scale
boundary_order: every old-anchor PV completes: ALL output columns and BOTH hi/lo components
U_ub = (U_ub + pending) * exp(a_old - a_new); factor is 1 for a held anchor
activate the next epoch; only NOW may new-anchor PV accumulate
route.group_predicate: two AIVs publish local decisions into DISJOINT SS byte slots (32 B aligned, 3 KiB model limit); the AIC reads both and ORs them into one group decision

theta_derivation.rule: theta_legal = max(0, min(log(dtype_max / P_HEADROOM), log(F32_MAX / (P_HEADROOM * block_c * |V|max))))
theta_derivation.why_not_6: the reference source's constant 6 is not a bound for any particular P dtype; for float16 the legal bound is about 9.70 at block_c=128, and for bfloat16 about 80.4. Copying 6 would be legal for one and arbitrary for the other

output_shard.note: the shard computes only its own columns and no merge happens between programs, which is G62's contract reached through this route

doc_two_block_example.note: scores 0 and 10 with V=1; a late old-anchor PV would give 1.9999 instead of 1.0

constant_max.note: a constant maximum must not trigger repeated drains

frequent_growth.note: monotonically rising maxima: the worst case for drains

tail_all_masked_row.note: an all-masked row reports zeros, not inf-inf

split_aiv_decision.note: the group decision is the OR of the two published local decisions; a one-sided read would give whichever AIV the AIC happened to read

final_flush.note: the route's final flush is the last boundary; a kernel that returns with pending still in L0C would omit that mass from U_total/l

conditional_guards.note: every deferred channel is CONDITIONAL on one published predicate; a conditional Set with an unconditional Wait, and two different predicates on the two sides, are both refused

completion_obligations.name: pv_all_columns_all_components_complete_e0
completion_obligations.why: every old-anchor PV must finish before the drain, for every output column and both hi/lo components; a stale P buffer does not imply this, because the P slot is legally free while the PV it produced is still in flight

completion_obligations.name: ss_decision_publish_both_aivs_e0
completion_obligations.why: each AIV writes disjoint SS bytes and the AIC reads both; the AIC's group OR is the only decision, so a one-sided read would be a silent disagreement

completion_obligations.name: group_predicate_visible_to_aic_e0
completion_obligations.why: the conditional drain and clear are guarded by the published predicate; SS is a scalar channel and carries no data-path completion of its own, so the read must be an explicit effect

completion_obligations.name: factor_survives_all_boundary_consumers_e0
completion_obligations.why: the per-row factors must stay live until the last consumer of the boundary finishes; overwriting them with the next boundary's values rescales at the wrong epoch

completion_obligations.name: l0c_clear_visible_before_new_anchor_pv_e0
completion_obligations.why: the new anchor's PV may only accumulate after the clear: L0C is clear/accumulate mode, so an unclear residue would be added into the new-scale accumulator

completion_obligations.name: pending_has_no_reader_until_drain_e0
completion_obligations.why: the canonical route's per-tile contribution transfer must NOT read L0C while the route is deferred; that transfer is exactly the cost this route removes

completion_obligations.name: pv_component_hi_complete_e0
completion_obligations.why: the hi and lo probability components are separate producers, so both must be in the completion set; folding them into one producer would let a drain proceed with half the contribution

completion_obligations.name: pv_component_lo_complete_e0
completion_obligations.why: the hi and lo probability components are separate producers, so both must be in the completion set; folding them into one producer would let a drain proceed with half the contribution

faults.effect_if_accepted: the group decision becomes whichever AIV wrote last, which is wrong exactly when the two disagree

faults.why: the AIC must read BOTH published decisions and take the group decision itself; reading one side is how a disagreement becomes silent
faults.effect_if_accepted: an AIV that needs a rescale would be outvoted by the one whose slot the AIC happens to read

faults.why: the group predicate says False but the anchors moved; a False predicate with a moved anchor would skip the drain and mix scales
faults.effect_if_accepted: the drain would be skipped while the accumulator scale changed, mixing two scales in one L0C accumulator

faults.why: an anchor may only grow or hold; a decreasing anchor would rescale the prefix UP and overflow
faults.effect_if_accepted: exp(a_old - a_new) > 1 would rescale the drained prefix UP and can overflow the output

faults.why: summing the rounded operand changes l by 0.00175207 on a 32-element block, which silently redefines the denominator
faults.effect_if_accepted: the normalisation would use the quantised weights, changing the numerical path the case doc fixes in P0

device_measurement.reason: The NPU measurement window is held by another teammate for this pass: npu-smi 25.7.rc1 shows a resident python process (pid 2862599, 868 MB) on NPU 0, and the package rule is one NPU measurement job at a time. A second measurement would corrupt both sets of numbers.
what_would_complete_it: an exclusive device window under flock /home/.tf_device0.lock
the deferred route compiled as a real MixedKernel with the SS publish/read and the conditional L0C clear/accumulate expressed as IR effects
the same 20 official MLA cases run through the original comparator
median kernel time per case for canonical vs deferred at theta=0 and a positive theta, with warmup, repeats and the device exclusivity rule
device_measurement.what_is_implemented_instead: the protocol object, its invariants, the SS byte-disjointness check, the conditional guard pairs, the completion obligations, and eleven fault injections that are all refused with distinct codes

not_claimed: No device Set/Wait completion is proven. The reference model this generalises says the same, and spec 03 says the device must establish the order through the target's own completion mechanism.
No device latency, no kernel time, and no device correctness for this route.
Python float arithmetic over small matrices is reference arithmetic, not FP16/BF16 emulation; the _cast rounding is a declared device for the hi/lo split only.
No claim that the deferred route is FASTER than canonical. That comparison requires the device window and belongs to the P7 search.
The theta comparison establishes the algebra and the drain counts, not a numerical error budget for a real kernel.

next_gate.G70: the search must include the deferred route as a real candidate with a real device measurement; it is not an optional entry that can be dropped once the canonical route passes
